messages.subject: Exponentially Modified Normal Distribution
parts:
This may be a silly question, but is there any reason why the Exponentially Modified Normal pdf is:

f(x | \mu, \sigma, \tau) = \frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{\pi}} exp\Big(\frac{\lambda}{2}(2\mu + \lambda\sigma^2 -2x)\Big) erfc\Big(\frac{\mu + \lambda\sigma^2 -x}{\sqrt{2}\sigma} \Big)

whereas on Wikipedia, the pdf is:

f(x | \mu, \sigma, \tau) = \frac{\lambda}{2} exp\Big(\frac{\lambda}{2}(2\mu + \lambda\sigma^2 -2x)\Big) erfc\Big(\frac{\mu + \lambda\sigma^2 -x}{\sqrt{2}\sigma} \Big)

i.e. Stan lambda is divided by sqrt(pi), in the Wikipedia formula by 2.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Exponentially Modified Normal Distribution
parts:
Thanks. That's a bug in the manual. The code in fact divides by
two (by subtracting log(2) on the log scale).

I've just updated the manual for the next release:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1081#issuecomment-69395564

- Bob
